newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA CONFIRM INTEREST IN VENABLES AS COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA CONFIRM INTEREST IN VENABLES AS COACH.

text.p: Australian soccer officials
confirmed on Sunday they had held talks with Terry Venables but
said the former England boss had not yet been signed as
Australia's new coach.
Soccer Australia (SA) spokesman Steve Speziale told
reporters SA chairman David Hill had held discussions with a
number of leading coaches on a visit to Europe over the past
week, including Venables, former Ireland manager Jack Charlton,
ex-Barcelona coach Johann Cruyff and former Leeds manager
Howard Wilkinson.
"There's no denying that David has spoken with (Venables),
but he's also spoken with Jack Charlton, Johann Cryuff and (he)
told me today that he had dinner with Leeds' Howard Wilkinson
last night," Speziale said.
Hill left Australia last week for a FIFA meeting in Zurich,
saying at the time he was happy to talk to anyone about the
Australia position after long-time coach Eddie Thomson quit last
month for Hiroshima in the Japanese J-League.
Speziale added that, while Venables was "very interested" in
the Australian job, a deal was yet to be finalised.
"I have spoken with David Hill this morning and his comment
at this stage is quite simply that we've got nothing to say,"
Speziale said.
Australian media reported last week that Venables could be
appointed under a novel job-sharing scheme that would allow him
to spend most of his time in Europe and monitor the form of
Australian players there in the lead-up to the 1998 World Cup.
Australia has over 100 overseas-based players, including
Aston Villa goalkeeper Mark Bosnich and Lazio sweeper Paul Okon.
A locally-based coach would also be appointed to take charge
of players drawn from Australia's domestic national league.
